verification.note: Glob finds six new files: frontend/src/components/__tests__/peakJump.shortcuts.test.tsx, player/__tests__/peakJump.shell.test.tsx, and MediaControls/__tests__/peakJump.{controls,order}.test.tsx, peakJump.strings.test.ts and peakJumpHarness.tsx. componentFixtureParity.test.tsx:331 contains "peak-jump". The declared touch points name only frontend/e2e-components/ for tests. docs/process/spec-and-design.md:41-43 defines touch points as 'where the change is planned to reach' and does not exempt tests. The finding is accurate as stated, but it is a process and documentation gap, not a behaviour defect.

MediaControlsContainer.tsx:96 gates jumpAvailable on `interactive`, and :142 publishes false in the effect cleanup. No peakJump unit test or e2e spec passes interactive=false to MediaControlsContainer: a Grep for 'interactive' in the peakJump tests and the peak-jump e2e specs finds nothing. The ad-break test (peakJump.controls.test.tsx:159) drives state.interrupted, which is a separate term at :95. In real use the gate matters: YouTubeEmbed.tsx:487 sets interactive = !adActive && !ended, so on the end screen (ended, not interrupted) only `interactive` hides the button and stops P. The remount test (peakJump.order.test.tsx:318-330) presses P only after remounting, and peakJump.shortcuts.test.tsx:199 tests the 'not consumed' path only through nickname=null. No test presses P while the controls are unmounted, so dropping the cleanup would leave P consumed with no effect and the suite would still pass.

GestureOverlay.tsx:73-102 renders boost-pill, then the mostWatched status, in one flex-col container. Grep: no peakJump test or e2e spec mentions boost or the speed pill. GestureOverlay.test.tsx tests boost-pill only, never mostWatched. So nothing covers the I5 'below the speed pill' order.
